findings.title: Invalid formatted-create encoding drops unvisited shares unwiped; current WASM retains a public quorum
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Before release, verify that supported library backup output and ended-owner cleanup meet their contract; no external secret compromise is claimed.

evidence.level: runtime baseline reproduced, plus source/independent challenge; fix not implemented

steps: Use a synthetic 16-byte secret, group threshold 1, group specs [2,3], a 32-byte fixed seed, and unsupported encoding 2 in create_sskr_shares_formatted.

By source order, the full share set is generated, first encode returns Err, and unvisited raw share buffers are ordinarily dropped. No memory inspection, native Rust build or WASM execution was performed.
reproduction.inputs: Public SSKR vectors or synthetic constants only.

findings.expected: Generated raw-share Vec allocations belong to the formatted call. Their owner lifetime ends on encoding refusal: no successful result or reusable plan justifies keeping them. Visited shares get UrShare Drop wiping and copied outer input/seed get error-path cleanup. Temporary/owned-array wiping claims apply to ended allocations, without requiring guaranteed whole-memory/OS erasure.
findings.observed: Coordinator fresh integrity-pinned current WASM instance, one 16-byte public-fixture secret, 32-byte fixture seed, group threshold 1, [2,3], encoding 2. Refusal: Unsupported SSKR share encoding. Exact-payload scan of 1,310,720 memory bytes reports first member 0 occurrences, second 1, third 1. The two distinct unvisited members meet the known 2-of-3 threshold. No successful create preceded the failing call in that instance.
impact: Confirmed post-refusal residuals for a public quorum; no actual-user secret, external attacker, unauthorized read, exfiltration or cross-realm compromise demonstrated.
No additional recovery was performed; quorum status follows fixture threshold and distinct member indexes.
Medium is for demonstrated ended-owner cleanup failure, not presumed key theft; no high/critical elevation or blanket erasure claim.
findings.recommendedFix: Validate ShareEncoding before Secret/generation inside the cleanup closure, ensuring refusal still wipes copied input/seed. Give every generated share a zeroizing owner before any fallible encoding step so future failures also clean unvisited items.
findings.requiredVerification: The supplied one-call probe suffices for this baseline; do not rerun it here. Later authorized verification should reuse it against canonically regenerated hash-bound bytes and add pre-call/control snapshots plus all-unvisited-member assertions. Log counts/digests rather than full memory dumps. No build is needed to probe the existing module.
findings.challenge: The unsupported code is correctly refused; late validation alone is not compromise. Absence of first-member payload is consistent with its wipe, not proof that all first-member copies were erased. Remaining full exact payloads prove dead-allocation residuals in this artifact, not merely that some buffers exist. Medium is defensible as a measured breach of best-effort temporary/owned-data cleanup, independently of any hostile-reader claim.

findings.title: Direct Bytewords conversion double-tags accepted current/legacy tagged UR input
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Scope reviewer identifies a source issue; release disposition belongs to the coordinator. No release checks were requested.

evidence.level: runtime baseline reproduced, plus source/independent challenge; fix not implemented

steps: Start with vectors/sskr-v1.json deterministic[0].shares[0], extract its untagged CBOR using urToTransport(...).subarray(0,-4).

Prepend current tag bytes [0xd9,0x9d,0x75] or legacy [0xd9,0x01,0x35], append a recomputed CRC32, and encode those bytes with the Bytewords minimal dictionary as a ur:sskr record. readShare accepts that input and canonically normalizes it.

Call bytewordsToUr(urToBytewords(taggedUr)). It reaches sharePayload with two tags; after skipping the first, header is 0xd9 rather than a permitted byte-string head, so it throws Invalid SSKR share byte string. The reproduction is source-derived and was not executed.

Both direct tagged UR-to-Bytewords-to-UR calls fail with Error: Invalid SSKR share byte string. Source urToBytewords keeps existing tag then prepends a second; parser expects byte-string after just one tag.
impact: Direct declared library converter can emit unreadable text for accepted input. No normalized CLI/export defect asserted.
Runtime probe calls urToBytewords directly; writeShare failure follows source delegation, not a separate probe.
